title: prefill-profile-discovery-and-quant-skeletonizer-cli
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces a tenant-aware prefill profile discovery CLI and an automated quant skeletonizer to bootstrap quant profiles for new workloads. Includes simulation/dry-run mode and telemetry hooks for unit-econ estimation.
description:
Summary: Add a new CLI tool (prefill-discover) and service library that scans recent inference traces to synthesize candidate prefill/batching defaults and a lightweight 'quant skeleton' profile to jumpstart quantization trials.
Motivation: many customers delay enabling quantization and batching optimizations because building safe, conservative defaults requires manual profiling and tuning. This PR automates the discovery step, letting tenant admins generate suggested prefill shapes, batch curves and a skeleton quant profile (per-layer candidates, quant bit hints, and fallback-safe flags) along with a simulated unit-econ impact report.
Changes include:
- New binary cmd/prefill-discover (Go) implementing a tenant-scoped discovery pipeline with sampling, fingerprinting, and dry-run simulation.
- Prefill discovery library pkg/prefill/discover.go containing traffic summarizers, batch-shape heuristics, and a candidate scoring function that balances latency SLO risk against cost savings.
- Quant skeletonizer tool tools/quant/skeletonizer.py (Python) that consumes a distilled model signature and token-distribution heatmap to emit an opinionated minimal quant profile (layer groups, target bits, per-layer safe-guard flags).
- Telemetry: added telemetry events (prefill.suggest, quant.skeleton.generated, prefill.simulation.report) with aggregated metrics to console/templates/prefill (dashboard snippets) and new tracing hooks in internal/tracing/prefill.go.
- CLI UX: supports --dry-run, --simulate-traffic, --tenant-id, --seed-profiles and outputs JSON suggestions compatible with the existing policy/importer.
- Safe-apply flow: a simulated apply path that runs microbenchmarks against a shadow pool (if available) and returns a unit-econ delta estimate (tokens/second, estimated $/1M tokens).
- Tests: unit tests and integration tests under test/prefill/* with a small synthetic-trace corpus and a CI smoke test that runs in 2m.
Why this approach: We want to reduce the time-to-first-savings for customers by delivering conservative but actionable defaults. The skeletonizer intentionally produces small, explainable quant steps (e.g., group-to-8bit on dense attention matrices, per-layer fallback path) so that the runtime can gracefully fall back on failure.

Migration/Apply guidance:
- Generated suggestions are intended for review by tenant admins. Use --dry-run to preview.
- The CLI emits two artifacts: suggestion.json (candidate defaults) and simulation_report.json (unit-econ delta with CI).
- To apply: pipe suggestion.json into existing policy importer (tools/policy/importer) or use the new --apply flag (requires --shadow-pool).
Rollout & safety:
- The skeletonizer marks layers with fallback flags so runtime will auto-fallback to float execution on mismatch.
- Prefill suggestions include conservative cache hints and per-route enable flags.
Observability:
- New telemetry events were added and dashboard snippets included. Ops can monitor prefills using the prefill.suggest and prefill.apply metrics.
Docs:
- Added docs/guide/prefill-onboarding.md with sample CLI flows and interpretation of simulation reports.
Performance:
- Local synthetic traces show median token/sec improvements of 12-23% for workloads with >60% seq-1 traffic; worst-case simulated median latency regression under the conservative defaults is <2% (90% CI).
Merge: Squash-and-merge after approvals.
Post-merge actions:
- Release-note draft added to release notes channel and docs PR scheduled to expand onboarding guide.
- Telemetry pipeline configured to accept new events.
- Backfill job scheduled to run discovery for a small set of pilot tenants next week.
Known limitations & future work:
- Current skeletonizer is model-agnostic and conservative; future work includes model-aware layer grouping (ENG-2011 follow-up) and an optional automatic canary rollout.
- Shadow-pool dependent features (microbenchmarks) are skipped when a shadow pool isn't present.
- More robust multi-tenant privacy guarantees to be added (PII-safe sampling).
Overall this PR creates the discovery + skeletonizer building blocks to accelerate tenant adoption of batching, caching and quantization defaults in a safe, observable way.
